# Clean up disk earlier, and clear out stale mixes on a timer

**File:** `services/api/app/storage.py` — the file that DELETES finished mixes.
**Risk score:** 48 / high. Route: **human-required** (not a one-tap).

## What is wrong today

The automatic clean-up only wakes up when your disk drops **below 2 GB free**.
That is already inside the zone where mixes start failing — the failure diagnosis
measured a 20.7% failure rate on a machine sitting near that line, and the same
songs passed 10 out of 10 once it had room. So today the app waits until it is
already broken before it tidies anything.

## What this changes

**1. It starts cleaning at 4 GB instead of 2 GB**, and tidies up to 6 GB. That
puts the clean-up *above* the line where things break, so it prevents the problem
instead of reacting to it.

**2. It clears out finished mixes nobody has touched in 7 days**, on a timer,
whether or not the disk is under pressure. Those are dead weight — nothing in the
app reads them, and if someone asks for one again it is rebuilt.

## What it deliberately does NOT do

It does not clean aggressively. A high floor (say 8 GB) would be constantly
deleting your render cache — and a repeat mix coming back in **0.03 seconds** is
the best thing about the app in a busy room. You chose to keep mixes instant, so
this reclaims space **without** spending that. Anything from the last week stays.

## What can go wrong, and what protects you

The only real danger is deleting something that cannot be rebuilt — an original
song, its separated parts, or its analysis. Those cost real money (Replicate) and
are gone forever.

The protection is unchanged and is the whole safety of this file: it deletes
**only** files whose names end in one of five known throwaway endings, only at the
top level of the data folder, never inside `listening/` or `tuning_renders/` or
`library/`. Anything it does not recognise is kept.

## Evidence, run tonight

- The **existing** disk-safety test suite was run against this exact change,
  loaded in memory without touching your real file: **15 passed** — identical to
  the current code's 15.
- A separate sandbox check on a real folder: a 10-day-old mix was removed, a
  1-minute-old mix was **kept**, and every original / stem / analysis / metadata
  file and everything in a subfolder survived untouched.
- **A real bug was caught doing this and fixed.** The first version wrote
  `min_age_secs = _EVICT_MIN_AGE_SECS` as a default. In Python that freezes the
  value at start-up, which silently broke the ability to change the safety window
  afterwards — 5 tests failed. Now resolved at call time. This is exactly the kind
  of thing that would have shipped quietly if this file were not gated.

## Honest limits

- Not run against your **real** data folder — only temp folders. The first real
  run should be watched.
- 7 days is a judgement call, not a measurement. Nothing measures how long a mix
  stays popular, because nothing records playback yet.
